title: Does Your Generalist Skill Optimizer Really Incentivize Agentic Tasks? Rethinking Skill Optimization via Bipartite Attribution
abstract: arXiv:2610.37201v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Skill optimizers adapt an agent to long-horizon tasks, such as repairing a terminal environment, by rewriting its skill, a natural-language procedure in its context, and keeping the edits that raise success on a small dev set. On such tasks success is noisy, so a gain on a small dev set does not show that an edit helps, and a success score does not show what the edit costs. We introduce BiPA, which replays an optimizer's acceptance rule on candidates identical to its seed to measure what selection alone reports, and records each episode as a bipartite graph of turns and the text they read to trace extra input tokens to the behavior behind them. Across three optimizers, three agentic benchmarks and two models, the learned skills succeed about as often as their hand-written seed, 0.1 points higher on average. translated_title: 你的通用技能优化器真的能提升智能体任务表现吗？基于二部图归因重新思考技能优化
translated_abstract: 技能优化器通过重写智能体的技能（即其上下文中的一段自然语言流程），并保留那些能在小型开发集上提升成功率的编辑，来使智能体适应长时程任务（例如修复终端环境）。在这类任务上，成功与否带有噪声，因此小型开发集上的提升并不能证明某次编辑真正有帮助，而且成功率分数也无法体现该编辑的代价。我们提出BiPA，它在与其种子完全相同的候选上重放优化器的接受规则，以测量仅凭选择本身所能报告出的结果；并将每个回合记录为“回合—所读文本”的二部图，从而将额外的输入标记（token）追溯到其背后的行为。在三个优化器、三个智能体基准和两个模型上的实验表明，学习到的技能的成功率与手写种子大致相当，平均仅高出0.1分。它们在开发集上的收益在测试时消失：即使在没有任何候选真正带来改进的情况下，仅在最多30个任务上保留多个候选中的最佳者也能报告出同样大小的收益。
tldr: 论文提出BiPA方法，揭示通用技能优化器的开发集收益主要源于噪声任务下的选择效应而非真实改进——学习到的技能在测试时并不比手写种子更好，且额外的输入标记还带来隐性成本。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces BiPA, which reveals that skill optimizers' reported gains largely stem from selection effects on noisy agentic tasks rather than real improvement—learned skills perform no better than hand-written seeds on test while incurring hidden token costs—by replaying acceptance rules on identical candidates and tracing costs via bipartite graphs.
